claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a high-temperature single-phase BCC alloy.
Phase stability after the high-temperature BCC state is governed by competition between a thermodynamic driving force for ordering and a kinetic barrier to transformation.
Al content creates a Gibbs-free-energy imbalance that provides the primary thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
Limited Al diffusivity creates the kinetic barrier to ordering at lower temperatures.
Slow cooling permits a diffusion-limited transformation into an ordered, likely B2, phase.
Rapid cooling preserves the high-temperature disordered BCC state by kinetically freezing in its atomic arrangement.
The proposed controlled intervention compares slow cooling and rapid quenching from an identical high-temperature starting state.
Rapid quenching is expected to suppress oxygen-diffusion-driven ordering.
Short-range order or nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates mediate the transformation.
Lowering temperature produces a configurational-energy instability, notably influenced by Al, that favors ordering.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic diffusion for nucleation and growth of ordered regions.
Slow-cooled samples will contain more ordered B2 material within a BCC matrix than rapidly quenched samples.
The extent of ordering increases with available diffusion time.
B2 ordering can be identified by XRD superlattice reflections and nanoscale ordered regions can be examined by TEM.
The proposed mechanism operates in a temperature window below a critical temperature where decreasing atomic mobility makes Al diffusion rate limiting.
Additional alloying or external mechanical stress may modify the relevant diffusion kinetics and lies outside the proposed boundary conditions.
No statistically significant ordering or phase-fraction difference between slow-cooled and quenched samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions attribute ordering to oxygen diffusion, whereas the hypothesis and mechanism consistently attribute the kinetic limitation and ordering process to Al diffusion. No role for oxygen is otherwise specified.
